business_summary.text: Stallion India Fluorochemicals manufactures and supplies industrial gases with a focus on specialty gases including helium and refrigerants.

call_points.text: 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance maintained for next three years
EBITDA margin expected to improve by 3-4% over medium term with new capacities
Khalapur helium plant almost ready, start-up next month; Mumbattu facility operational by August.
Refrigerant demand in India and globally expected to grow 10-15% a year for the next 10 years.
H1FY27 margins strained by LPG cost and geopolitical disruption; management says it planned ahead.

classes.description: As per notes, As per notes

guidance.statement: These strategic initiatives, along with backward integration into manufacturing, are expected to support our targeted revenue CAGR of 30–35% over the next 3 years while improving margins by 3-4%.

status_history.evidence: Management reiterated the 30-35% revenue CAGR target over the next three years with 3-4% margin improvement.

guidance.statement: FY27 PAT expected at about ₹100 Cr, including ₹60 Cr from six months of R-32 output at 22% PAT margin.
Revenue CAGR of 30-35% over the next three years with margin improvement of 3-4%.
Target of ₹3,000 Cr revenue and ₹500 Cr PAT by 2030.
With R-32 fully operational, turnover should cross ₹1,100-1,200 Cr with about ₹180 Cr PAT.

industry: Commodities > Chemicals > Chemicals & Petrochemicals > Industrial Gases

operating_notes.text: Company operates in a single business segment of manufacture of industrial gases, so no segment disclosures are reported.
Net IPO proceeds unutilised at March 31, 2026 were temporarily invested in fixed deposits with banks, the Monitoring Agency Bank Account, IPO Escrow account and the company's current account.
The company proposed a 10,000 MT R-32 manufacturing facility at Bhilwara, Rajasthan, with environmental clearance received and commencement expected by October 2026.
R-32 plant capacity is 10,000 MT; the company expects a matching 10,000-ton quota and says the Indian R-32 market is about 20,000-22,000 tons, so output is aimed at exports and HFO blending.
Helium prices have risen to ₹3,000-4,000 per unit from ₹800-900 four to five months ago, which management calls an opportunity for its Khalapur entry.
The Mumbattu facility was scaled up 2.5 times from the IPO plan to a 12-tank facility covering HFO and HFC blending, de-bulking and helium and semiconductor gas handling.
Khalapur helium plant (1200 MT/annum) expected to contribute ~12% to FY27 revenue with PAT margin >15%
R32 plant revenue guidance for FY27 revised down to ~₹125 Cr (from ₹275 Cr) due to delayed commissioning and lower realisations (~₹800/kg vs ₹500/kg guidance)
HFO plant CAPEX expected to be ₹350-400 Cr with 10,000 ton capacity
Maharashtra GST officials conducted an inspection/search under Section 67, leading to voluntary reversals of ineligible ITC.

timeline.summary: Stallion India Fluorochemicals announced board approval to vary IPO proceeds utilization and noted the resignation of an independent director.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹109.99 Cr (-27.4% YoY), net profit ₹10.93 Cr (-17.6% YoY).
Stallion India Fluorochemicals reported FY26 total revenue of ₹434.12 Cr and PAT of ₹43.84 Cr.
Stallion India Fluorochemicals Limited’s **Govind Rao** shared the earnings conference call recording (18-May-2026) for Q4FY26 results via provided link.
Stallion India Fluorochemicals released the monitoring agency report for Q4FY26 detailing deviations in IPO proceeds utilization.
Stallion India Fluorochemicals' Q4FY26 earnings call guided FY27 PAT at about ₹100 Cr, with the R-32 plant starting by October 2026 and a 2030 target of ₹3,000 Cr revenue.
Stallion India Fluorochemicals shareholders approved a special resolution on 3 June 2026 to vary the objects of its IPO proceeds utilization.

Q1FY27 results: revenue ₹124.7 Cr (+12.8% YoY), EBITDA ₹25.27 Cr (+75.9% YoY); Khalapur helium plant to commence commercial operations in coming quarter; R32 plant commissioning delayed to December 2026
On 15 October 2026, Stallion India Fluorochemicals disclosed a Maharashtra GST search and inspection concluding on October 14, 2026, with voluntary ITC reversals.

watchlist.response: Said the dilution was due to the rights issue price of ₹99 versus the expected ₹140, and that the shares sold were bought back; holding is 47.5% or more.
watchlist.text: Promoter sold rights entitlement to a DII despite saying he would apply, and holding fell to 44%.

watchlist.response: Said the FY26 internal target was ₹430 Cr revenue and ₹40 Cr PAT, which was surpassed; the 30-35% growth applies from FY27 onwards.
watchlist.text: FY26 revenue grew only 14% against the 35% CAGR target, and Q4 revenue fell 27% QoQ.

watchlist.response: Said volumes fell because end-customer industries could not get LPG and ran below full production due to the geopolitical situation.
watchlist.text: Why has the top line stayed flat at ₹105-110 Cr for four quarters despite a 15-20% rise in product prices?

watchlist.response: Said the government will announce it in FY27 and the company expects 10,000 tons; declined to comment on the method.
